# LayoutPanel

Header: `winui/ui/panels/LayoutPanel.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/panels/LayoutPanel.hpp`.

A panel whose measure and arrange are delegated to an attachable [Layout](../controls/item-layouts.md#uilayout).

Use it for a fixed set of children with a layout that no built-in panel offers. That is a custom [NonVirtualizingLayout](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-nonvirtualizinglayout), or a [StackLayoutEngine](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-stacklayoutengine), [TileLayoutEngine](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-tilelayoutengine), [WrapLayoutEngine](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-wraplayoutengine) or [LinedFlowLayoutEngine](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-linedflowlayoutengine) applied to ordinary children, where every child counts as realized. [Border](border.md#uiborder) and padding come off the room before the layout sees it. With no layout, every child fills the whole content box, stacked on top of each other.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative:
window.set_content(ui::LayoutPanel{
    .layout   = ui::TileLayout{},
    .padding  = ui::Thickness{12.0f},
    .content  = {ui::Text{.text = "A"}, ui::Text{.text = "B"}, ui::Text{.text = "C"}},
});

// Imperative:
auto  panel = std::make_unique<ui::LayoutPanelControl>();
auto* stack = panel->set_layout(std::make_unique<ui::StackLayoutEngine>());
stack->set_spacing(8.0f);
panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("First"));
panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Second"));
panel->set_padding(ui::Thickness{12.0f});
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

## `ui::LayoutPanel`

Children measured and arranged by a [Layout](../controls/item-layouts.md#uilayout) object. Builds a [ui::LayoutPanelControl](#uilayoutpanelcontrol). The panel takes ownership of [`.layout`](#uilayoutpanel-layout); reach it again through [`.control`](#uilayoutpanel-control)'s [layout()](#uilayoutpanel-layout).

The counterpart of [ui::ForEach](../controls/for-each.md#uiforeach) for hand-written children: every child is realized, and any [ui::Layout](../controls/item-layouts.md#uilayout) (a stock one or the app's own subclass) places them.

Example: 
```cpp
auto grid = std::make_unique<ui::TileLayoutEngine>();
grid->set_min_row_spacing(8.0f);
grid->set_min_column_spacing(8.0f);

window.set_content(ui::LayoutPanel{
    .layout   = std::move(grid),
    .padding  = ui::Thickness{12.0f},
    .content  = {
        ui::Button{.text = "One"},
        ui::Button{.text = "Two"},
        ui::Button{.text = "Three"},
    },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::LayoutPanel{
    .layout, .background, .border_brush, .border_thickness, .corner_radius, .padding, .style,
    .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height,
    .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled, .accessibility,
    .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down,
    .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

| <span id="uilayoutpanel-corner_radius"></span>`corner_radius` | `ui::Binding<float>` | `{0.0f}` | Corner radius, DIPs. |

## `ui::LayoutPanelControl`

Derives from `ui::Panel`, `ui::LayoutOwner`.

A panel whose measure and arrange are delegated to an attachable [Layout](../controls/item-layouts.md#uilayout).

Use it for a fixed set of children with a layout that no built-in panel offers. That is a custom [NonVirtualizingLayout](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-nonvirtualizinglayout), or a [StackLayoutEngine](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-stacklayoutengine), [TileLayoutEngine](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-tilelayoutengine), [WrapLayoutEngine](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-wraplayoutengine) or [LinedFlowLayoutEngine](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-linedflowlayoutengine) applied to ordinary children, where every child counts as realized. [Border](border.md#uiborder) and padding come off the room before the layout sees it. With no layout, every child fills the whole content box, stacked on top of each other.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative:
window.set_content(ui::LayoutPanel{
    .layout   = ui::TileLayout{},
    .padding  = ui::Thickness{12.0f},
    .content  = {ui::Text{.text = "A"}, ui::Text{.text = "B"}, ui::Text{.text = "C"}},

// Imperative:
auto  panel = std::make_unique<ui::LayoutPanelControl>();
auto* stack = panel->set_layout(std::make_unique<ui::StackLayoutEngine>());
```


### add

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* add(std::unique_ptr<T> child)
```

Takes ownership of `child`, appends it after the existing children, and returns a non-owning observer. Updates the layout.

### add

```cpp
template <SpecLike S>
Element* add(S&& spec)
```

The declarative overload: builds `spec` (or takes the node a [ui::Spec](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#class-spec) holds) and adds it as [add()](#add) does a control. Returns the built node as an [Element](../tree/element.md), or nullptr for an empty [ui::Spec](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#class-spec), which adds nothing; a spec's `.control` field gives a typed observer.

### set_layout

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_layout(std::unique_ptr<T> layout)
```

Takes ownership of the layout, destroying any previous one, and returns an observer to it. nullptr leaves the panel with none.

### layout

```cpp
Layout* layout() const
```

The current layout (non-owning), or nullptr when the panel has none.

### parallel_measure_safe

```cpp
bool parallel_measure_safe() const override
```

True without a layout, otherwise what the layout answers ([Layout::parallel_measure_safe()](../controls/item-layouts.md#parallel_measure_safe)).

### border_brush

```cpp
std::optional<Color> border_brush() const
```

The outline color; nullopt (the default) draws no border even with a non-zero [`border_thickness()`](#border_thickness). Nullopt as well while a [ThemeColor](../tree/theme-color.md) is set.

### border_brush_resource

```cpp
ThemeColor border_brush_resource() const
```

The theme resource the border is drawn from, or null.

### border_thickness

```cpp
const Thickness& border_thickness() const
```

The border width in DIPs per side (default zero); it insets the children like padding.

### corner_radius

```cpp
float corner_radius() const
```

The corner radius in DIPs, uniform for all four corners (default 0, square).

### padding


The padding in DIPs between the border and the children (default zero).

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.
